title: Headless Emergency Radio (VEFR01NCRGood2EmergencyRadio): an NCR radio operator finds a player the NCR likes and hands over the emergency radio; the radio calls a supply drop (stage 10); the supply cache opened (stage 20)

actions.text: Path: with NCR fame (given; good tier >= 2) and no faction armour on, the quest script, while the player is outdoors in the region vMapCanSupportPCHere, moves the radio operator (VEFR01NCRRadioOperatorRef) near the player with a talk-to-player package; his greeting gives the emergency radio (bHasRadio: the radio added); used, the radio's effect sets bUsingRadio and the quest's MenuMode shows the radio's menu; button 1 calls a supply drop, which over the next menu-mode passes places a supply cache by the player (stage 10); the cache's OnActivate sets 20 (completes; the stages repeat, one call a day).
Stand-in for walking into the region: the player at Nipton's map marker (the Wasteland), then SetPos to a point inside one of the region's polygons (REGN 0x0015F432).
Stand-in for his talk-to-player package (AddScriptPackage is a stub, dialogue packages start no conversation headless): the operator starts the conversation.

The radio is used from the Pip-Boy (menu 1002 open: the quest's MenuMode runs), its menu answered with button 1 (a supply drop), and the Pip-Boy kept open for the drop's menu-mode passes (ten seconds: the button's ResetQuest also drops the quest's SetQuestDelay 0.1, so the next MenuMode pass waits the default 5 s; whether the original's ResetQuest resets the delay is not known, see the report).

Back into the region before the radio is used: the box shows its call buttons only while IsPlayerInRegion vMapCanSupportPCHere (MESG 0x0016663C button conditions); the walk to the operator, who stands about 6000 units off, left it.
The cache the drop placed (PlaceAtMe: a reference made at run time, named created:).
